The biased estimate is non-negative and 0 for identical samples; the unbiased estimate is reported as computed, including negative values. p = (1 + #{permuted statistic >= observed}) / (1 + B) is a valid p-value under exchangeability of the pooled sample. Dense Gram matrices: the smaller dimension should stay below a few hundred. The measures summarize a spectrum; they do not say which directions matter for a task, and the cutoff for zero singular values affects nearly rank-deficient matrices.
Guarantees

With k equal non-zero singular values, the effective rank, participation ratio and stable rank all equal k; a rank-one matrix gives 1. All three are invariant to orthogonal transformations of rows or columns and to scaling the whole matrix. 1 <= effective rank <= numerical rank.
Assumes
The scale of each feature is meaningful; the measures change if features are rescaled unequally. Singular values at or below 1e-12 times the largest are treated as zero.
items.summary: Measure how many directions a representation matrix actually uses: the effective rank (exponential of the entropy of normalized singular values), the participation ratio of the eigenvalues and the stable rank. Use it to detect collapsed embeddings or compare the dimensionality of learned representations.
items.title: Effective rank, participation ratio and stable rank

cases: PSR against zero ignores that this series was the best of 20 tries; in the seeded test the best of 20 pure-noise strategies passes PSR > 0.95 in over 30 percent of runs.
items.name: deflated_sharpe_ratio
notes: Limits

Asymptotic: with few observations or heavily dependent returns the PSR is approximate. The deflation needs the number of effectively independent trials and the variance of their Sharpe ratios, both of which must be estimated honestly (every configuration tried counts). The expected-maximum formula is an approximation to a Gaussian extreme value. It does not test for other forms of overfitting such as look-ahead bias.
Guarantees

PSR(SR* = SR) = 0.5 exactly; PSR increases with the number of observations when SR > SR*. expected_maximum_sharpe scales with sqrt(variance) and stays within 0.05 of the exact Gaussian expected maximum for 10 to 1000 trials (checked by quadrature). Invalid inputs (zero variance, fewer than 2 trials, a non-positive variance term) raise ValueError.
Assumes

Returns are i.i.d. with a finite fourth moment; the PSR relies on the asymptotic normality of the estimated Sharpe ratio. trials is the number of effectively independent configurations tried, and their Sharpe ratios are roughly Gaussian with the given variance. All Sharpe ratios are per period (not annualized) and in the same units as the variance.
items.summary: Compute the probability that a strategy's true Sharpe ratio exceeds a benchmark given skewness, kurtosis and sample length, and deflate it for having picked the best of many trials by comparing against the expected maximum Sharpe ratio of pure-luck trials. Use it before reporting the best of a configuration search.
items.title: Probabilistic and deflated Sharpe ratio

cases: An unweighted score counts each clone as a separate member; with conserved weights the two clones are one member.
items.name: weighted_vendi_score
notes: Limits

Dense eigendecomposition by Jacobi rotations: intended for at most a few hundred members. Eigenvalues at or below 1e-12 are treated as zero, which matters for orders below 1. The score depends entirely on the chosen kernel; it says nothing about quality, coverage of a target distribution or usefulness of the members.
Guarantees

n mutually orthogonal members with equal weights score n; identical members score 1. Splitting a member into identical clones whose weights sum to its weight leaves the score unchanged. The score lies between 1 and the number of members with positive weight and does not increase with the order q.
Assumes
The similarity matrix is a valid kernel: symmetric, positive semidefinite, with k(x, x) = 1. Weights express how much each row counts; rows with weight 0 do not affect the score.
items.summary: Measure the effective number of distinct members in a weighted set from a similarity matrix or feature rows. Use it to compare the diversity of samples, prompts, solutions or ensemble members when members carry unequal weight or appear as duplicates.
items.title: Weighted Vendi score

cases: Counting messages, a receives its own observation back and counts it as a second, corroborating one.

Every report either is a root observation or names the reports it rests on; the provenance links are complete and honest. Two root observations are independent of each other; the tool cannot detect a shared hidden cause.

items.name: mechanism_heldout_split

Greedy fold assignment balances task counts approximately, not optimally. Holding out whole mechanisms leaves fewer, larger test units, so estimates have more variance than task-level splits.
Guarantees

split_by_mechanism holds out k = max(1, min(M - 1, floor(fraction M + 0.5))) whole mechanisms chosen by a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle of the sorted names; no mechanism is on both sides. group_k_folds partitions every task and every mechanism into exactly one fold, assigning mechanisms largest first to the least loaded fold. leakage lists every mechanism present on both sides of a split.

cases: The Hebbian sum v1 k1^T + v2 k2^T retrieves 0.6 for k2 because k1 and k2 overlap; the delta rule removes that crosstalk for the latest pair.
items.name: delta_rule_associative_memory
notes: Limits

Dense matrices for small key and value sizes (tens to a few hundred). Sweeps converge slowly when keys are nearly parallel. With more pairs than key dimensions the pairs cannot all be stored; sweeps then cycle instead of converging, and least_squares_memory refuses dependent keys. No forgetting, gating or decay terms are modelled.
Guarantees

After a delta update with rate * ||k||^2 = 1, retrieving k returns v exactly (up to rounding). Writes with keys orthogonal to k leave the retrieval of k unchanged. With unit keys and rate 1, sweeps from zero converge to least_squares_memory when the keys are independent; divergence raises ValueError.
Assumes
Keys and values are real vectors of fixed length; the memory starts at zero in store_pairs. Exact one-shot storage needs rate * ||k||^2 = 1; stability needs 0 < rate * ||k||^2 < 2.
items.summary: Store key-value pairs in a matrix with the error-correcting update M <- M + rate (v - M k) k^T, retrieve with M k, and compare with the Hebbian rule and the minimum-norm memory. Use it to test fast-weight or linear-attention memories for interference and capacity.
items.title: Delta-rule associative memory

The flow on edge (u, v) means flow from u to v; reversing an edge's orientation negates its value. Which 3-cycles count as filled is a modelling choice: declared triangles or every 3-clique.

items.name: anytime_confidence_sequence
notes: Limits

Means of bounded observations only; the bounds must be known in advance. The Hoeffding sequence is conservative; the betting sequence is tighter but costs grid x n operations and is meant for up to a few thousand observations. Grid reporting rounds intervals outward by at most one cell. Guarantees need a constant conditional mean; under drift the sequence covers no single target.
Guarantees

hoeffding: P(mu leaves the interval at some t) <= alpha, by Hoeffding's inequality at level alpha / (t (t + 1)) and a union bound. betting: the averaged capital (K+ + K-) / 2 at the true mean is a non-negative martingale, so P(it ever reaches 1 / alpha) <= alpha by Ville's inequality; the reported intervals contain every candidate mean the capital never rejects. Running intersections keep the simultaneous guarantee; empty_at records a time when the intersection would have become empty.
Assumes
Observations lie in the stated bounds and share one conditional mean given the past (for example independent and identically distributed). The level alpha is fixed before looking at the data.
items.summary: Give confidence intervals for the mean of bounded observations that hold at every time simultaneously, so results can be monitored after each run and stopped at any point. Includes a Hoeffding union-bound sequence, a betting (hedged capital) sequence and a seeded coverage simulation.

items.name: split_conformal_intervals
notes: Limits

Marginal coverage only: it does not guarantee coverage for each input value, and under distribution shift the guarantee is lost. items.name: ledoit_wolf_shrinkage
notes: Limits

Single target (scaled identity); other targets such as constant correlation or a diagonal are not included. The intensity is an estimate of the loss-minimizing value with an asymptotic guarantee, not the oracle intensity for a given small sample. Dense p by p matrices: meant for p up to a few hundred.
Guarantees

shrinkage = min(bbar^2, d^2) / d^2 lies in [0, 1]; it is 0 when the sample covariance is already a multiple of the identity. With shrinkage > 0 and a positive target scale the estimate is positive definite, even when p > n. Scaling the data by c scales the estimate by c^2 and leaves the shrinkage unchanged; rotating the data rotates the estimate.
Assumes
Observations are independent and identically distributed with finite fourth moments (the setting of the consistency result). The sample covariance divides by n, as in the Ledoit-Wolf derivation.
items.summary: Shrink a sample covariance toward a scaled identity with the Ledoit-Wolf intensity, giving a well-conditioned, positive definite estimate even when there are fewer observations than variables. Use it before inverting a covariance of metrics, features or embeddings estimated from few runs.
items.title: Ledoit-Wolf covariance shrinkage

items.name: normalize_and_recover_email_addresses
items.summary: Clean and repair email addresses: remove mailto and angle brackets, lower the case, repair spelled out at and dot, doubled punctuation and mistyped domains such as gmail.con, and refuse cells with several addresses or an invalid shape.
items.title: Clean and repair email addresses

items.name: normalize_website_addresses
items.summary: Normalize website addresses (URLs): add a missing scheme, write the scheme and the host in lower case, optionally remove www, remove a trailing slash, and keep the path, query and fragment exactly as written. Invalid hosts go to review.
items.title: Normalize website addresses

items.name: normalize_whitespace_and_unicode_text
items.summary: Normalize whitespace and Unicode in text fields: non-breaking spaces, tabs, doubled spaces, split accents, zero-width characters and typographic quotes. Folding accents, umlauts and other diacritics to ASCII is an explicit choice and never a default.
items.title: Normalize whitespace and Unicode in text fields

items.name: profile_text_column_before_cleaning
items.summary: Profile a text column before cleaning it: count case, whitespace, Unicode, email, website, phone and legal suffix signals, find the common character patterns, and propose cleaning rules with the evidence for each. Changes no data.
items.title: Profile a text column before cleaning it

items.name: propose_a_dedupe_without_deleting_rows
items.summary: Turn duplicate pairs into clusters and a merge proposal with one survivor for each cluster, keep first or keep most complete, without deleting any row. Possible pairs become review questions with two choices.
items.title: Turn duplicate pairs into clusters and a merge proposal with one survivor for each cluster

items.name: restore_capitalisation_of_names
items.summary: Fix the capitalisation of person and company names written in all upper case or all lower case: particles such as van and de, Mc and Mac prefixes, acronyms such as IBM and LLC, with a confidence for each value and review for doubtful ones.
items.title: Fix the capitalisation of person and company names written in all upper case

items.name: score_duplicate_pairs_by_weakest_signal
items.summary: Score whether two records are the same entity (fuzzy matching): build comparison keys for name, address, email and phone, measure token overlap and sequence similarity, and let the weakest field set the confidence. A shared email alone never merges two records.
items.title: Score whether two records are the same entity

items.name: split_address_lines_into_components

items.title: Parse a postal address line into house number
